alt: Component 4 is worth 85 marks: a research report of up to 5000 words worth 75 and a research log worth 10. The assessment objectives are weighted AO1 65%, AO2 20% and AO3 15%. The research proposal form is also submitted but not externally marked.
caption: The report carries most of the marks, and research and evaluation carry most of the report.

after: ## Choosing and framing the research question
alt: Three versions: industrialisation is a topic, not a question; has industrialisation been environmentally damaging is a question but one-sided; is industrialisation a good thing works because it opens competing views. Below, a scale from too broad and shallow to too narrow with too little evidence, with the best fit in between.
caption: The title must be a question that opens a debate, sized to the evidence available.

alt: The research proposal form sets out the research question, key concepts, an outline of the debate and example sources. The teacher checks relevance, scope and safety and formally approves it. It is sent to Cambridge but not externally marked.
caption: The unmarked proposal shapes the question, and the question shapes every mark.

after: ## Perspectives, evidence and the literature review
alt: A perspective is a coherent world view responding to an issue, made of argument, evidence and assumptions. Primary evidence is first-hand and lets you test claims but small samples rarely generalise; secondary evidence gives expert depth but may share hidden assumptions. A literature review groups sources into perspectives and assesses each.
caption: Build perspectives from argument, evidence and assumptions, and weigh both kinds of evidence.

alt: A table of four research methods with a strength and a limitation each: literature review, interviews, surveys and close analysis of texts. Below, qualitative evidence gives depth in words and meanings; quantitative evidence shows patterns in numbers.
caption: Every method trades depth against breadth; justify the trade you make.

alt: The research log is worth 10 marks, kept separate from the report and outside the word count. A weak log only records dates and searches. A strong entry, from week 6, notes what was found, why it matters, the decision made and the next step.
caption: Each log entry should record a decision, not just an action.

after: ## Structure, referencing and the word limit
alt: The report runs from an introduction explaining how the question was developed, through a main body of methods and compared perspectives, to a conclusion that judges and reflects, then a bibliography in one consistent referencing system. It is continuous prose of at most 5000 words with the count stated.
caption: Introduction, body, judging conclusion and full references, within 5000 words.
